long_biography.plain_text:
Puerto Portals began as Klaus and Margarita Graf's plan for a marina unlike those then operating in Spain. Permissions and construction took six years, required land reclaimed from the sea and even a quarry for the foundations, before the complex opened in 1986. Margarita later recalled that it took another three years for local boat owners to embrace the harbour.

The project joined marina services with restaurants, boutiques and year-round leisure, establishing a model that helped reshape Mallorca's nautical tourism. After Klaus Graf's death, Margarita and their daughter Corinna continued in the family's island companies; public registry records place both women in joint administrative roles. Corinna assumed day-to-day leadership of Puerto Portals, while Margarita retained a governance role within the wider family business structure.

uncertainties.detail: Public reporting generally uses Margarita Graf, while Spanish registry records use Margarita Bimboese von Trott zu Solz or compressed variants. The shared Klaus and Corinna Graf family links, direct Puerto Punta Portals presidency, German-Mallorca context and later joint company roles establish that these names refer to the same owner. Unrelated German care, cosmetics and automotive executives named Margarita Graf were excluded.

Later profiles often foreground Klaus Graf as Puerto Portals' promoter, but Mallorca Magazin directly calls Margarita the founder and quotes her detailed recollection of development and adoption; Economía de Mallorca identifies both spouses as founders in their daughter's anniversary remarks. The dossier therefore uses co-founder rather than sole founder.

Margarita ceased to be a direct Puerto Punta Portals director and president in 2017, when Ailana Cubed and Atira Investment became corporate directors. September 2026 registry records show Margarita and Corinna jointly administering those vehicles, while separate July 2026 filings identify Corinna as Atira's sole shareholder. No reviewed source discloses Margarita's present beneficial interest in the marina or the complete family holding structure, so the biography describes governance rather than ownership or day-to-day management.

Shipping & Maritime is used as the required origin-sector fallback. Puerto Portals remains Margarita's defining business identity and the corporate-vehicle records support a continuing family-governance link, but the current weights of marina, hotel, agriculture, property and investment assets are not public.

Mixed reflects two positive components: Margarita's directly evidenced co-founder and development role, and the pre-existing industrial fortune and Mallorca investment programme of husband Klaus Graf. The sources do not allocate individual capital contributions, ownership percentages or inheritance, so the dossier does not classify the wealth as purely self-made, purely transferred or inherited.

Forbes was searched first and no dedicated profile was found. Focused searches of LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok and personal websites produced either no result or unrelated namesakes. Only the official Puerto Portals Company Website is proposed.

Marina operations is the minimum useful active tag and directly satisfies its founder/developer membership rule. Broader Shipping or Hospitality tags are omitted as overlapping proxies, while inactive Marina operator is not assignable. No catalogue candidate is created.

No reliable source reviewed establishes Margarita's precise birth date or year, birthplace, middle names as structured by the owner form, secondary nationality, secondary residence or personal website. German nationality, Spain residence, German birth country, female gender and Alive status already exist in the authoritative record and are not reproposed.
